## Definition

The **independent variable (IV)** is the variable that the researcher manipulates or selects to examine its effect on the dependent variable. It is the presumed *cause* in a cause-and-effect relationship.

## Key Characteristics

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Manipulated | Researcher controls the levels |
| Presumed cause | Expected to influence the DV |
| Has levels | Different conditions or values |
| Comes first | Temporally precedes the DV |

## Levels/Conditions

The IV has different **levels** (also called conditions):

| IV | Levels |
|----|--------|
| Caffeine | Present vs. Absent |
| Music type | None, Classical, Pop |
| Teaching method | Traditional, Active, Online |
| Drug dosage | 0mg, 50mg, 100mg |

## Experimental vs. Measured IVs

| Experimental IV | Measured IV |
|-----------------|-------------|
| Actively manipulated | Naturally occurring |
| Random assignment possible | Participant characteristic |
| Stronger causal inference | Weaker causal inference |
| Example: Drug vs. placebo | Example: Gender, age |

## Identifying the IV

Ask: "What is being manipulated or compared?"

> "Does **caffeine** improve memory?"

IV = Caffeine (levels: caffeine vs. no caffeine)

> "Is there a difference in anxiety between **students and workers**?"

IV = Occupation (levels: student vs. worker)

## Multiple IVs

Experiments can have more than one IV:

```
Factorial Design: 2 × 2

IV1: Caffeine (yes/no)
IV2: Sleep deprivation (yes/no)

Creates 4 conditions:
1. Caffeine + Sleep
2. Caffeine + No sleep
3. No caffeine + Sleep
4. No caffeine + No sleep
```

## DataLab Connection

At the **Frontal Lob** station, the IV is trial type (congruent vs. incongruent). At **Lady Luck**, the measured IV might be risk preference. Always identify whether the IV is manipulated or measured.
